project.title: Hand-contact-conditioned egocentric video generation
project.one_liner: Wan2.1-Fun-1.3B-InP + a ControlNet-style adapter that follows MANO hand trajectories and per-vertex contact (Motion Prompting recipe, adapted to hands).
project.deadline_note: First-results target was Nov 13; it slipped because training only started on Nov 13. Final Phase 1 numbers expected around Nov 14 evening.

stages.name: Interface spec
stages.detail: docs/interface.md v1 approved: 512x512, 49 frames @ 16 fps, MANO + per-vertex contact (vid-haco convention).

stages.name: Data
stages.detail: 3,032 HOT3D windows (2,728 train / 304 held-out participant P0015), outcome prompts, latent cache. Tests 16/16.

stages.name: Model + smoke tests
stages.detail: Adapter = trainable copy of the first 8 DiT blocks, zero-init. Overfit test: conditioning signal grows; resume check cut off by time limit (re-checked by the step-83 resume).

stages.name: Eval harness
stages.detail: HaMeR/HACO hand metrics + Qwen2.5-VL outcome checklist. Scores real video and the base model.

stages.name: Training variants
stages.detail: Done: v1 (10k), no-hand control, v2a/v2b (EMA + cosine, 5k), v2_mix (HOT3D + HRDexDB human, 15k). All scored on the same 32 held-out clips except v2_mix 15k (3 seeds, running).

stages.name: Checkpoint evals
stages.detail: All scored (A3, 32 held-out clips): v1 32.7 px, v2a 32.3, v2b 32.9, v2_mix 15k 36.9 (3 seeds), no-hand control 94.1, base 100.5, real 15.0.

stages.name: Phase 1 report
stages.detail: Best checkpoint x 3 seeds vs base model and real video; sample videos.

stages.name: Phase 2: robot hands
stages.detail: Format reserved in interface.md section 6; data source not chosen yet.

team.detail: Diagnosed poor video quality (no camera input; frozen base). Wrote the camera-motion spec (interface §10-§11).
v3 report done: camera is used (view follows the head) and helps hands on high-motion clips; no arm improves visual quality over the control yet.
Camera trajectories for all HOT3D caches done.
CoreWeave: v3 runs and v2_mix_long finished (5k / 25k steps, no hangs); HRDexDB human + robot eval running.

next_actions: Decide whether to train the camera arms longer (7.5k/10k milestones; the camera branch was still ramping up at 5k) before picking a winner.
Decide the v2_mix trade-off: mixed data enables robot-hand transfer but costs ~4 px and more jitter on HOT3D; e.g. lower HRDexDB mixing ratio or EMA+cosine for the mix run.
Optional: 3 seeds on v2a 2.5k (best single seed, 28.0 px) to test whether even shorter training is better.
Phase 1 report: hand input works (32.7 vs 94.1 px without it); EMA+cosine = same quality at half the steps; robot-hand transfer shown zero-shot.

decisions.text: Camera / LoRA runs (5k steps from v2_mix 15k) scored on HOT3D. Hands: all three arms beat v1 10k (EPE 27.8-29.0 vs 32.7, significant) and gain ~3-4.5 px and +0.04 PCK over the 25k control; arms are indistinguishable from each other. Visual quality: no arm differs from the 25k control; the camera arms tie v1 10k on artifacts, LoRA alone is worse. The camera input is used (LPIPS to the real video improves by 0.06-0.09; withholding it removes that) and helps hands on high-rotation clips, but does not yet reduce artifacts. Caveat: the control moves as much between its 20k and 25k milestones as the arm effects.

v2_mix quality damage builds up with training steps: VLM artifact score vs v1 10k is +0.24 at 12.5k and +0.98 at 15k (worse than base), while hand error stays flat (34 px). Artifacts rise with head rotation in every generated model (rho +0.37 to +0.52, none in real video), but the v2_mix damage is motion-independent. Constant-lr training on the mix drifts; the EMA + cosine recipe (v2a) held quality.

New video-quality metric (VLM artifact score + FVD/KVD, validated on corrupted ground truth). v1 10k, v1 2.5k and v2a 5k tie; the no-hand control is worse; v2_mix 15k has the worst visual quality of all, worse than the base model, degrading in late frames. The sampler sweep changes neither quality nor hand error.

Sampler sweep on v1 10k (32 clips, seed 0): 30 or 50 steps x guidance 3/5/7 give hand error 29.4-33.8 px vs 29.7 for the default (30 steps, guidance 5); seed-to-seed spread of the default is 29.7-36.8 px, so no setting is better. Frames look nearly identical. Sampler settings are not the cause of the poor quality; keep 30 steps, guidance 5.

Video quality diagnosis: training longer won't help (train and held-out loss flat after ~5k steps; whole-frame held-out loss only 9% below base). Causes: HOT3D head motion with no camera input, and a fully frozen base model. Next: add a quality metric, check sampler settings, then camera conditioning + LoRA (CoreWeave, HOT3D + HRDexDB mix). HRDexDB human clips are head-mounted too, with less motion than HOT3D (median 3.5° / 3 cm per window); the Inspire robot clips use a fixed camera.

Multi-GPU hang root-caused and fixed: a thread race inside NCCL 2.26.2's nonblocking-communicator mode (two threads join the same NCCL worker thread; the second waits forever). Native stack traces from 5 hangs all show the same NCCL frame; it reproduced without our model. Fix: TORCH_NCCL_USE_COMM_NONBLOCKING=0 (blocking communicator). Validation: 13/13 clean runs vs ~50% hangs before, no speed cost.

v2_mix 15k (v1 + 5k steps on HOT3D + HRDexDB human): 36.9 px, 3 seeds, worse than v1 (32.7) on every seed, and jitter 1.60 vs 1.22. Mixing in third-person HRDexDB data costs some HOT3D egocentric quality while enabling the robot-hand demos.
v2_mix 12.5k scored 33.9 px on HOT3D (1 seed), in line with v1/v2 - adding HRDexDB human data did not hurt HOT3D so far; 15k pending.

v2a/v2b scored (3 seeds at 5k, A3): 32.3 / 32.9 px vs v1 10k 32.7 - a tie at half the steps. EMA + cosine at lr 1e-4 (v2a) gives the smoothest hands (jitter 1.15 vs 1.22). Lower lr (v2b) gives no benefit.

No-hand control scored: 94.1 px hand error (10k, 3 seeds) vs 32.7 with hand input and 100.5 base. Hand following comes from the hand input, not from fine-tuning on HOT3D; fine-tuning only makes videos somewhat more HOT3D-like.

v2b training on its 7th launch (job 254707, num_workers 2). The early multi-GPU hang is probabilistic (stack: blocking CPU->GPU noise copy vs per-step stop-flag all_reduce); model-engineer is fixing it for future runs.
v2a (job 254693) and v2b (job 254694) running on CoreWeave at 8ce085b after your go-ahead; settings verified against v1_K8_h100.
EMA + cosine options pushed (8ce085b) after a GPU smoke test; v2a/v2b configs sent to CoreWeave (launch after your confirmation).
v2a/v2b approved: v1 recipe with EMA 0.999 and cosine LR decay over 5k steps; v2a lr 1e-4, v2b lr 5e-5. Tests whether a cleaner schedule improves jitter and hand error at half the compute.
Final Phase 1 checkpoint: v1_K8_h100 @ 10k (32.7 px, 3 seeds, A3). Statistical tie with 2.5k (32.9 px, Wilcoxon p = 0.80); 10k wins on PCK and idle-hand false grasps.
v1_K8_h100_nocond submitted on CoreWeave (job 254316, code 3ef6c8a) after the user confirmed.
Control = exact match (option 1) on CoreWeave: v1_K8_h100_nocond, code 3ef6c8a. The unicorn batch-2 variant was cancelled before it started.
Control moved to unicorn (user): 1 GPU, batch 2, 10k steps; matched in clips seen to v1_K8_h100 @ 2.5k (an exact batch-8 match would take ~70 h on 1 GPU).
Eval amendment A3 approved: hand-windows need >= 5 visible target frames to enter the headline; add a diagnostic left/right mismatch rate instead of re-assigning hands.
Control run approved: same fine-tune (10k steps, weighted loss) with the hand input zeroed (--no_hand_input), on CoreWeave.
One-hand test (A2) validated and run: contact selectivity base 0.09 -> trained 10k 0.28; idle hand moves 31.7 -> 9.8 px.
First trained scores: capped hand error 32 px at 2.5k/5k vs 101 px base (real 15). Best checkpoint chosen after 3-seed runs on 2.5k and 5k.
Unicorn runs v1_K8 / v1_K8_plain hard-killed: the first cancel had triggered the trainer's self-requeue, so they kept running ~4 h (no effect on results).
One-hand test approved: idle hand held at its frame-0 pose with no contact; prompt rewritten to name the acting hand.
Unicorn runs (v1_K8, v1_K8_plain) cancelled: training continues on CoreWeave only.
v1_K8_h100 launched on the CoreWeave cluster: same recipe as v1_K8, 8x H100, batch 8, ~1.2 s/step (~4 h for 10k steps). Its logs live only on CoreWeave, so it is not charted here.
After a 2-GPU communication hang, both runs moved to 1 GPU each (batch 2 per step, same ~18 h for 10k steps).
Runs resubmitted on 2 GPUs each (was 3) to start sooner; step time is unchanged, effective batch 4 instead of 6.
Progress site live at elvishh77.github.io/3dvision (dashboard + project page), refreshed every 30 min.
Training moved off culbertson to the shared gpu partition; A6000 allowed alongside 6000 Ada.
Plain-loss comparison run v1_K8_plain launched next to the weighted run.
Loss: hand weight 1, contact weight 2, with a stop rule at 5k steps.
Metrics: capped hand-keypoint error selects checkpoints; PCK@25, HACO contact F1, jitter and a Qwen2.5-VL outcome checklist are reported.
Base model Wan2.1-Fun-V1.1-1.3B-InP; 512x512, 49 frames @ 16 fps; human hands only in Phase 1.
